review: Request: Moss asked for a physically grounded, repeatable way to compare a food sample's mass before and after air exposure, with stated resolution and limitations, instead of treating the visible shrinkage of his root slice trial as measured water loss; he carried one stone, had seen branches and loose stone sources of untested suitability, and knew of no calibrated balance. World Agent decision: develop (learning 4) a general operation to assemble and use a lever mass comparator with material ids, support ids, a sample id, a reference id and modes assess, assemble, test, compare, inspect and dismantle; the smallest physical version is a rigid beam on a stable fulcrum with a repeatable seat and a movable reference, without cords, pans, machining or calibrated weights; torques come from actual conserved masses and lever arms including the beam's own weight, pivot resistance and contact failure are resolved in code, and observations show only visible tilt, displacement, slip, damage and null ranges; costs are study 4 rounds at 0.5 energy, assess 1 round at 0.2, assembly 3 rounds at 0.5, each reading 1 round at 0.2, a validity test of at least three empty and three loaded readings from both tilt directions, endpoints of at least three loaded readings bracketed by empty checks, and dismantling 1 round at 0.2, with no reward. Implemented: lever-mass-comparator@1 (handler long.lever-mass-comparator, equivalence measurement:lever-comparator:reference-mass-ratio:1, study 4 rounds at 0.5 energy). assess (1 round, 0.2 energy, nothing else changes) reports each requirement met or missing for named materialIds, supportIds, referenceId and sampleId, naming the missing physical prerequisites, or the physical setup of any reachable comparator by comparatorId. assemble takes materialIds [beam: the person's own whole untreated fallen-branch unit; optional fulcrum: an own whole sound stone or flint unit set on firm ground where the person stands] or one supportIds entry (a solid unreserved stone or flint object in reach) and referenceId (an own non-food, non-decaying, untreated piece of at most 1 unit); it costs three paid rounds of 0.5 through workCreate and workPay that continue each round (seat the fulcrum, lay the beam, set the reference); the parts are reserved in place and then moved with their exact ids and records from the person's inventory into a new non-solid lever-comparator world object, so they add no carried weight and the assembly mass is the sum of its parts; an unworked round pauses it without charge and assemble with comparatorId resumes after rechecking reach, reserved parts, support and energy. test and compare are paid readings of 1 round and 0.2 energy, empty or loaded (sampleId: an own unreserved item of at most 1 unit, seated and taken back within the round and never consumed or altered), with an outward or inward approach: the reference slides from the far end of its slide until the beam tips, which happens where the gravitational torque of the actual masses (reference x position minus sample x seat arm plus beam weight x centre-of-mass offset) exceeds the pivot stiction g x 0.005 m x the total mass on the fulcrum, so the two approaches bracket a null range; the tip is reported to the nearest 0.02 of the half-beam with +/- 0.02, or as tipped at the start or no tip within the slide. A test passes when at least three empty and three loaded readings of one sample, each set from both directions, repeat within 0.04 and close; it records the empty and loaded null ranges, hysteresis, reload spread and the interval sample/reference = (loaded null - empty null)/(0.9 +/- 0.02), never below zero; otherwise the comparator is invalid until a new test passes. compare on a tested comparator: an opening empty check, at least three loaded readings of one sample from both directions and a closing empty check within 0.04 of the tested baseline (otherwise invalid for drift) give an endpoint interval relative to the reference; a later endpoint of the same sample, followed through base pickup, thin-slice cutting and air-exposure placement by their own events, and the same reference gives an after/before interval, reported as a decrease or increase only if it excludes 1 and otherwise as inconclusive, with observed quantity changes; it states that it is net mass change only, not water loss, contamination, preservation, safety or a cause, and that repeatability is not absolute accuracy. inspect (1 round, 0.2) reports the comparator and the person's own readings; dismantle (1 round, 0.2) stops unfinished work, releases its reservations and returns every part with its identity. Every refusal spends nothing; only the assembler may test, compare, inspect, resume or dismantle, while anyone in reach may assess; at the owner's death unfinished work stops, unplaced reserved parts lie at the death position, the comparator stays where it stands unowned and anyone in reach may dismantle it, and its readings give nobody knowledge or permission. Unattended effects: an unworked assembly round pauses; rain at an outdoor comparator marks it visibly wet once per wet spell and voids its test, so a new test is needed; a fulcrum piece whose ground stops being firm damages the comparator (physical failure event; only dismantling remains). Events lever-comparator-assessed, -progress, -paused, -resumed, -assembled, -reading, -tested, -invalid, -endpoint, -compared, -inconclusive, -inspected, -wetted, -failed, -dismantled and -interrupted carry view metadata (constituent ids, position, beam endpoints and orientation, fulcrum contact, seat and reference positions with their uncertainty, tilt, work progress, validity state with the labels assessed, assembling, untested, tested, invalid, damaged and dismantled, linked event ids, no badge); the object reuses the existing loose-material drawing and the work rounds the existing process-progress events; results go to the person's reading record and unverified openRemember records, never as grams, masses or water content. Modeling assumptions: one whole fallen-branch unit is a straight uniform rod of the declared branch-screen@1 rod length 1.1 m laid across the fulcrum at its visible midpoint, so its centre-of-mass offset is 0 and its own weight acts at the fulcrum and adds to the pivot load; taper is not represented and only branch has a represented piece length, so other beams are refused; mass units are read as kg; positions are fractions of the half-beam judged by eye against the beam ends, the fulcrum and the seat, with a visible resolution of 0.02; the seat is fixed at 0.9 of the half-beam on the seat side and placed within 0.02, and the reference slides from -0.8 to 0.95; the pivot stiction is an effective rolling-resistance arm of 0.005 m (half an assumed 0.01 m contact width, well below the 0.033 m beam diameter), the documented bounded parameter that sets the hysteresis and with the visible resolution the resolution, equal in both directions and for item and object fulcrums; bending strength and stiffness use the material-geometry@1 wood values restated (dry density 600 kg/m3 with the resource moisture as water share, modulus 4e9 Pa, strength 45e6 Pa) for a round section derived from the beam's mass, so loads of at most 1 unit never visibly bend or break it and heavier loads would be refused before any charge; loads stay seated because rolling and sliding are not represented; placement is deterministic, so the reload spread is zero unless the physical state changes; non-food materials have no water exchange in this world, so rain changes no represented mass, but a wetted stone or flint reference is bounded by 1% surface water in comparisons and any other wet reference makes a comparison inconclusive; stone and flint are the represented hard rigid fulcrum materials and non-food, non-decaying items the stable references; drop and pickup move whole units only, so references are whole items such as a second branch. Reuse: a registry check found no installed or installable interface in this scope that weighs or compares masses; the ex10 food-assay@1, assay-woven-supports@1, measured-food-preservation@1 and noningestive-extractability@1 balances belong to scope open-ex10, need vine pans, calibrated weights and mastery and are not argument-compatible, so none is reused; reused are BRANCH_SCREEN_GEOMETRY, the material-geometry@1 wood values, long-ex19-material-contact.ts (contact and firm-ground checks), collective-work.ts, openRemember, foodUnitMass, forestClimate rain, forestResolveReference and the loose-material drawing. food-air-exposure-trial@1 and thin-slice-food-drying-trial@1 are byte-identical, their instrumentId stays refused (tested with a standing comparator), and a sample lying in one of their trials is used only after the person's own base pickup, which pauses or ends that trial under its own rules. A throwaway check on the archived round-64 world, since deleted, confirmed Moss's real items: assessment named only the missing beam; with a branch gathered from canopy-41, the outcrop start-2-stone as fulcrum and stone item-38-moss-458 as reference, the test passed with root item-26-moss-307 at 0.11 to 0.30 of the reference, and the picked-up dried slice item-48-moss-575 gave 0 to 0.16 of it. This is not a first release: the specification is self-consistent and the world represents every item's mass, so the comparator is a simplified but real mechanism with real costs, real state (a placed assembly holding its parts and readings in the person's records) and observable events; no practice milestone, satisfaction or comfort is granted, the practice evidence event carries no qualified flag, and this run's incentive channel is off.
